citation: "Chicago's First Post Office." Chicagology, transcribing J. Seymour Currey, "U. S. Government and Post Office Buildings," Fort Dearborn Magazine, December 1922.
note: Source for: the post office established at Chicago 31 March 1831 with Jonathan N. Bailey as postmaster; the office kept 'in a log building about where South Water street intersects Lake street, near the east end of the bridge', with John S. C. Hogan keeping a store in the same building; Bailey succeeded by Hogan 2 November 1832; Sidney Abell appointed 3 March 1837 and the office removed in May of that year to Bigelow's Building on Clark. Also the only statement reached that gives the Thompson 1830 plat's street width as a uniform 66 feet with 16-foot alleys, which DISAGREES with the 80-foot figure annotated on Hathaway 1834 and used by this project's placement offsets. WHERE IT DISAGREES WITH ANDREAS, ANDREAS IS FOLLOWED: this page has Hogan moving the office to 'the south west corner of Franklin and South Water streets' on succeeding Bailey in November 1832, while Andreas says twice, in two independently written passages, that the office stayed at Lake and South Water until about July 1834 and gives the building's size there. See docs/RESEARCH/hogan_store.md § 3.
